slideDifferences.nativeText:
IDIOM
MEANING
EXAMPLE
GIVE SOMETHING A SHOT
To have a try at something.
I have never eaten sushi, but I will give it a shot.
HAVE A BONE TO PICK
An unpleasant issue or grievance that need discussion.
I have a bone to pick with you about that email.
GO FOR BROKE
To risk everything and go for an all out effort.
If you decide to go for broke, you can’t be thinking about what will happen if you fail.
MAKE A CLEAN SWEEP
To remove all unwanted people or things in order to start afresh.
The new leaders wanted to make a clean sweep of the discredited old order
GIVE THE NOD
To show one's approval of someone or something.
I gave Amanda the nod because she is the most qualified candidate.
HAVE AN AX TO GRIND
To have a private reason for doing or being involved in something.
He has no political axe to grind.
GO-TO GUY/GAL
The person is frequently asked for help in that topic.
Amanda’s our go-to gal for computer issues.
MAKE A KILLING
To earn a lot of money in a short time and with little effort.
They made a killing with the sale of their London house.
Look at the information, listen to your teacher and repeat the words. Discuss about them.

B. Listen to the audio and answer the questions your teacher makes.
Work-life balance

I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances or if I need to make an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes without having dinner to finish a task. It can also get quite lonely working on my own, and I sometimes miss sharing ideas with colleagues.

Adapted from https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/reading/upper-intermediate-b2/work-life-balance

texts: 1. Have– used to talk about food, drink, washing, resting talking.
2. Take – Used to talk about washing, resting, decisions, problems, care.
4. Go - Used with verbs to do with moving. Also, with nouns that do not have an ing form, we use the structure ‘go for a’
5. Do - Used with nouns in ing that have to do with work. Additionally, with nouns when it is obvious what the action is.
6. Give - Used with noises, facial expressions, hittings, affectionate actions, talking.
7. Adjectives are used to add extra information to the action we want to express.

texts: B. Listen to the audio and answer the questions your teacher makes.

I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances or if I need to make an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes without having dinner to finish a task. It can also get quite lonely working on my own, and I sometimes miss sharing ideas with colleagues.
